mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine typically costs £1,100-£2,400 supply-only, depending on power output and supplier. EP6DT 150hp units start around £1,100, while 5FY 175hp units range £1,300-£2,400. Used engines start from £700. Supply & fit adds £450-£900 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £4,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine problems are high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure causing hard starting and misfires, timing chain stretch and tensioner failure causing cold-start rattle, carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection, and turbocharger oil feed line leaks. The 5FY 175hp variant is particularly susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 207 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With 207 1.6 THP values typically £2,000-£6,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,100-£2,400 represents a significant investment but often makes sense for well-maintained GTi and RC models. For sub-£2,500 examples, a used engine from £700 may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 207 1.6 THP (EP6DT/5FY) engine can reach 100,000-130,000 miles. However, HPFP failure can appear as early as 50,000 miles, and timing chain issues from 40,000-80,000 miles. Regular oil changes with correct PSA-approved oil, timely timing chain replacement and HPFP monitoring are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 207 1.6 THP 150 and 175 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.6 THP 150 (EP6DT, 5FX) produces 150hp and was fitted to GT and Sport trims. The 1.6 THP 175 (5FY, EP6DTS) produces 175hp and was fitted to RC (GTi) models. Both use the same 1.6L Prince architecture, but the 5FY has a higher-output calibration, larger turbocharger and more aggressive engine mapping. The 5FY is also more susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear due to higher cylinder pressures.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine code is EP6DT (5FX) for 150hp models or 5FY (EP6DTS) for 175hp models. It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 207 1.6 THP - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 207 1.6 THP was the performance flagship of the 207 range, bringing turbocharged power to the compact hatchback. Powered by the Prince engine family - jointly developed by PSA and BMW - the 1.6 THP (Turbo High Pressure) delivered up to 175hp in the GTi and RC models. First introduced in 2008, the 1.6 THP featured twin-scroll turbocharging, direct injection and advanced engine management, making it one of the most exciting hot hatches of its era. However, its complexity and well-documented reliability issues - particularly high-pressure fuel pump failure, timing chain stretch and carbon buildup - have made it a growing source of replacement enquiries for owners of the 207 GT, GTi and RC.

milestones.description: **2008** - 1.6 THP 150 (EP6DT, 5FX) introduced for GT and Sport trims, producing 150hp
**2009** - 1.6 THP 175 (5FY, EP6DTS) launched for RC (GTi) models, producing 175hp
**2010** - Minor ECU refinements to improve cold-start behaviour and fuel mapping
**2011** - Timing chain tensioner revisions introduced to address early failures
**2012** - HPFP and turbo oil feed line updates for improved reliability
**2013** - 207 production ends; 1.6 THP continues in 208 GTi and other PSA models

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every EP6DT and 5FY engine fitted to the Peugeot 207 1.6 THP is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 207 1.6 THP Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 207 1.6 THP (EP6DT/5FY) is a thrilling engine when running well, but its Prince architecture - shared with BMW and Mini - has well-documented weaknesses. High-pressure fuel pump failure, timing chain stretch, carbon buildup and turbocharger issues are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. The 175hp 5FY variant is particularly susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear. Every rebuilt Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why Peugeot 207 1.6 THP Engines Fail to Start and Run Roughly
problems.rootCause: The Bosch HPFP's internal cam follower wears prematurely, causing metal contamination to circulate through the high-pressure fuel rail and injectors. Symptoms include hard starting, rough idle, misfires and, in severe cases, complete non-start. The issue is particularly common on the 5FY 175hp variant due to higher fuel pressures.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace pump, flush fuel lines, replace inline filter
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught before metal debris reaches injectors

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full rebuild with upgraded HPFP and cleaned rail, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Essential when metallic particles have contaminated the combustion chambers

problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the Peugeot 207 1.6 THP is catastrophic if delayed. If diagnostic codes show fuel rail pressure deviation alongside metallic fuel, budget for a full engine replacement immediately - repairing injectors alone will not prevent repeat failure. The 5FY 175hp variant is especially susceptible; HPFP failure is one of the most common reasons for 207 GTi engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Find specialist Peugeot 207 1.6 THP rebuilt engines with upgraded HPFP

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why Peugeot 207 1.6 THP Engines Rattle on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The Prince engine's timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack to develop. Over time, the chain stretches and the plastic guides wear, leading to rattling on cold start and, in severe cases, chain jump and valve-piston contact. Peugeot released a TSB with revised tensioner and guide parts.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner (revised), guides and VANOS sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, new HPFP and turbo seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 207 1.6 THP exhibits the characteristic cold-start rattle, address it immediately. A timing chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the rattle is constant or accompanied by loss of power, the chain has likely jumped - at that stage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine prices with upgraded timing components

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup - Why Direct Injection Causes Power Loss and Rough Idle
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not wash the intake valves with fuel, allowing carbon deposits from the PCV system to accumulate on valve stems and seats. This restricts airflow, causing rough idle, hesitation, reduced power and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before valve damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with refreshed valvetrain and intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if carbon buildup has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a known characteristic of direct injection engines. A professional walnut blast cleaning every 40,000-60,000 miles is a worthwhile preventative measure. If the engine has been running poorly for an extended period, carbon scoring may have damaged cylinder walls - in which case a rebuilt unit is the only reliable fix.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Peugeot 207 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger & Oil Feed Issues - Additional Vulnerabilities
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger's oil feed line can leak or become restricted, starving the turbo of lubrication and leading to bearing failure. Carbon deposits in the turbo can also cause wastegate sticking. The 5FY 175hp variant places additional stress on the turbo system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of turbocharger and oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new turbo and oil feed system
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 207 1.6 THP has turbo lag or blue smoke, have the oil feed lines inspected immediately. Replacing these components early can prevent catastrophic turbo failure. Once turbo debris has contaminated the oil system, a full rebuilt engine is the safest option.
